learning_outcomes.text: Understand the functioning of companies both from an organizational point of view and from the accounting representation of their results, up to assessing the aspects of strategic management.

Understand the concepts of business and competitive environment, with specific reference to the sectoral structure, the definition of business, competitive dynamics and the basic outlines of business strategies.
Understand the differences and characteristics of competitive and growth strategies, methods of implementation.
Understand the criteria of strategic coherence and the basic models of organizational design.
Understand both the functioning of a company and the environmental context in which it operates.
Identify the most appropriate competitive strategies and implementation methods.
Experiment with an integrated reading of company functions and their use for competitive purposes.

Formalize judgments on the different conditions of attractiveness of a sector, and to evaluate the most appropriate strategies and the interests that converge in the company and principles of governance.

Communicate the knowledge acquired clearly and concisely; correctly and appropriately use language, concepts and models acquired to effectively discuss the possible managerial solutions adopted and adoptable by companies.

Independently update knowledge relating to business management and the use of strategy in light of the ongoing evolutions and changes that will occur in the extended and competitive environment in which a company operates.

syllabus_topics: The actors and the features of organizations
The stakes involved in the business activity and their satisfaction
teaching_methods: Discussions of concrete sector and business examples

assessment_methods.method: Open-ended questions (2 questions) on the specific topic

assessment_rules: The exam consists of 24 closed multiple choice questions and 2 open-ended questions. Multiple choice questions have four answer options, only one is correct, and there is no penalty for incorrect answers. Grading is based on a Final Mark.
